Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a controls mapping spreadsheet and a short evaluation annex that covers regression approach, traceability, and EU AI Act positioning. High-level notes below; details are in the attachments.

Quick overview:
- NIST AI RMF mapping: we map our operational controls to the five core functions (Govern/Map/Measure/Manage/Respond) and include control owners, evidence artifacts, and ownership of monitoring alerts. See tab "RMF_Mapping" in the spreadsheet.
- Regression strategy: we run nightly sampled regression jobs for production models (stratified by route/tenant when applicable), plus a weekly full-batch smoke test on commit for major model changes. Metrics: ROUGE/BLEU where applicable, task-specific accuracy, hallucination rate estimates derived from rule-based detectors, latency and token-cost drift. Failures trigger an automated canary rollback policy and a ticket to the model release owner.
- Traceability & retention: every request tied to a model invocation stores immutable metadata: model_id, model_hash, quantization_profile, prompt_id, input_hash, KV-cache-exception flags. We retain prompt/response logs for 365 days by default; longer retention options available under Dedicated/Private. Audit export includes per-request trace id, model binary checksum, and policy annotations.
- EU AI Act stance: Redwood markets inference-as-a-service. We provide tools and exportable artifacts to help customers demonstrate compliance (model inventories, risk-tier annotations, evaluation sampling results). For high-risk classification, customers often operate in Dedicated/Private modes and sign custom SOW items for conformity testing. Redwood is developing an optional conformity annex for customers that need to declare deployment-level mitigations.

Excerpt — Evaluation & Regression approach:

1) Sampling strategy
- Production sampling: we stratify by route, tenant, and input-length buckets. For high-risk routes we sample at higher fixed rates and keep deterministic sample seeds for reproducibility.
- Pre-release sampling: every model variant entering canary is evaluated against a weighted prompt-set derived from customer-provided prompts and open-source benchmarks.

2) Metrics tracked
- Functional correctness: task-specific metrics (F1, exact match, ROC AUC for classification).
- Safety regressions: false positive/false negative rates of guarded classifiers, toxicity score deltas, hallucination incidence (rule-based heuristics + human-in-the-loop samples).
- Performance & cost: p50/p95 latency, tokens-per-response distribution, effective throughput under expected concurrency.

3) Regression gating and rollbacks
- Canary window: automated monitoring collects evaluation metrics and user-feedback signals for the canary cohort. If metric delta crosses a pre-defined threshold we automatically route new requests to the previous stable variant and create an incident.
- Human validation: for ambiguous regressions we run a human review sample and freeze rollout until sign-off.

4) Artifacts for audits
- Model inventory exports (model_id, training_data_digest, fine-tune manifest if applicable), per-release eval bundles (sample seeds + metrics), and per-request trace logs.
- For Dedicated/Private customers we can provide hashed dataset provenance records and signed attestations for releases.

5) Operational notes
- Quantization: we version quantization profiles and include performance/capability matrices for each profile.
- KV-caching and prefix caching: cache keys are maintained per model_id + schema_version and included in the trace export for reproducibility.
